newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU urges Angola's UNITA to commit to peace process.
newsitem.headline: EU urges Angola's UNITA to commit to peace process.

text.p: The European Union on Thursday urged Angola's opposition UNITA movement to meet its obligations to the country's peace process quickly if it wanted to avoid sanctions threatened by the United Nations Security Council.
The U.N. has given UNITA until August 15 to fulfil the conditions of the deal or risk seeing more, unspecified, measures taken against it.

"It is the view of the European Union that further failure on UNITA's part to meet their obligations will almost certainly make unavoidable the imposition of additional measures as outlined in earlier Security Council Resolutions...," the Luxembourg EU presidency said in a statement.
The opposition movement reached a peace accord with the Luanda government in 1994 after nearly two decades of civil war.
The U.N. has already banned sales of arms and fuel to UNITA. New sanctions could hit UNITA travel and banking.

The EU said UNITA's delay in meeting obligations agreed under the 1994 peace deal reached in the Zambian capital Lusaka was "calling into serious question the genuineness of its commitment to the peace process".
"The European Union calls upon UNITA to demonstrate clearly that such fears are unfounded by meeting its remaining tasks without further delay," the presidency statement added.
UNITA, a former rebel movement, has failed among other things to integrate territories it controls with those of the government, and to demobilise its fighters.
UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi was, however, reported on Tuesday by Portugal's Lusa news agency to have offered to hand over territory still under the movement's control by November.

The EU said it was also disturbed by persistent tension in areas of Angola and in particular called on the Angolan government and UNITA to refrain from using force, in accordance with their Lusaka commitments.
